full_judgment:
Mr. K.M. Hasan, J : The Petitioners seek leave to appeal against the judgment dated 25.8.2002 passed by a single Bench of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 3631 of 2000 discharging the rule. 

2. The facts leading to the leave petition arc that respondents as plaintiffs instituted Fide Suit No. 31 of 1994 for permanent injunction restraining the defendant' petitioners from dispossessing the plaintiff respondents from the suit land.

3. The case is that the suit land originally belonged to one Hari Charan Mondal and Ramgati Mondal and on the death of Ramgati Mondal. Hari Charan Mondal became the sole owner of the suit land . While in possession Hari Charan Mondal died leaving behind only son Ram Krishna Mondal and the S.A. Khatian was prepared and finally publiShed in the name of Ram Krishna Mondal. The latter died leaving behind 4 sons. (Upendra Chandra Mondal. Muktinda Chandra Mondal. Jatindra Chandra Mondal and Panchannan Chanrda and by a family arrangement Upendra Chandra Mondal got the entire suit land measuring .30 decimals and his other brothers got other lands in other Khatians. While in possession the said Upendra Chandra Mondal sold the suit land to one Rustam Ali on 22.4.1969 by a registered Kabala. Rustam Ali mutated his name and sold .15 decimals of land by three registered kabalati on 24.12.1985 to Abdul Hamid Mahmud. Sharif Mahmud and Hasan Mahmud. The three purchasers by registered kabala dated 2.3.1991 sold the said .15 decimals of land to one Mr. Mobarak Hossain who again appointed Moharak Hossain as constituted attorney. The latter subsequently sold the entire .15 decimals of land to the plaintiffs. His further case of the plaintiff respondents is that Rustam Ali sold his remaining .15 decimals of land in favour of the plaintiff Nos.1 and 2. The plaintiff respondents mutated their names in Mutation Case No. 3336 of 1986 and have been possessing the suit land by constructing boundary wall As the defendants threatened the plaintiffs with dispossessing hence they filed Title Suit No. 31 of 1994 for permanent injunction . 

4. The defendant petitioner's case is that the suit property originally belonged to Ramgati Mondal and Hari Chandra Mondal. One Dehendra Chandra Mondal heir of Ramgati Mondal and Hari Chandra Mondal sold .60 decimals of land on 21.8.1952 from the suit plot to Ahmed Hossain and Nor Mohammad and put them in possession. During S.A. operation the names of Ahmed Hossain and Nor Mohammad was recorded. Subsequently by two separate registered kabalas on 16.7.1980 they transferred .30 decimals of land in favour of defendant Nos. 2 and 3 and put them in possession. His said defendant petitioners appointed defendant No. 4 as the caretaker and since the plaintiff respondents assaulted defendant No. 4 on 2.3.1994 and drove him out of the suit property the defendant petitioners instituted a criminal case against the plaintiff respondents. The petitioners further case is that they are possessing the suit land by constructing boundary wall and the document of the plaintiff' respondents are forged and collusive.  

5. The trial court on consideration of the evidence found that the plaintiff respondents could not prove their title and dismissed the suit by judgment and decree dated 11.4.2000. 
6. The plaintiff respondents then preferred Title appeal No. 40 of 2000 and the appellate court allowed the appeal by its judgment and decree dated 29.6.2000. 

7. Against that judgment the defendant petitioners moved the High Court Division in its revisional jurisdiction in Civil Revision No. 3631 of 2000 and a rule was obtained which was subsequently discharged on the finding that the defendant could not prove their prima facie title and exclusive possession in the suit land, the documents filed by the plaintiff respondents are not forged and the plaintiff respondents have proved the existence of' a boundary all on all sides of the suit land which did not in any way discard their exclusive possession. 

8. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners could not show any illegality or infirmity in the judgment of the High Court Division calling for our interference. 

End.
